title: VideoToolbox glue for the H.264 encoder
done: vt/n2avc_vt.h: exactly one declaration, OSStatus n2avc_vt_create(uint32_t, CFAllocatorRef, VTVideoEncoderRef *), weak_import on iOS and plain on -DN2_HOST_FAKE.

vt/n2avc_vt.c: static n2_CMBaseClass (version 1, derivedStorageSize sizeof(struct n2avc_vt), finalize, copyDebugDescription, copyProperty, setProperty, rest NULL) and static n2_VTVideoEncoderClass (version 1, startSession, encodeFrame, completeFrames, copySupportedPropertyDictionary, rest NULL) and the {NULL, base, class} vtable.

n2avc_vt_create: rejects codec types other than 'avc1' with -12902, CMDerivedObjectCreate with VTVideoEncoderGetClassID, per-object pthread mutex, property dictionary, defaults (30/1, four slices per the lead's real-time edit, CQP 26, keyint 60).

startSession: stores the unretained session token and dimensions; rejects width/height outside 16..4096 x 16..2304 and odd sizes with -12902; announces 420v+420f in a CFArray plus width, height and an empty IOSurfaceProperties dictionary.

All 29 properties from TASK.md: AverageBitRate, ExpectedFrameRate, MaxKeyFrameInterval, MaxKeyFrameIntervalDuration, RealTime, Quality, NumberOfSlices, N2Threads and DataRateLimits are decoded into n2avc_config; ProfileLevel, AllowFrameReordering, AllowTemporalCompression, H264EntropyMode, ColorPrimaries, TransferFunction, YCbCrMatrix, PixelAspectRatio, CleanAperture, FieldCount, MaxFrameDelayCount, Priority, SourceFrameCount, ExpectedDuration, BaseLayerFrameRate, EncoderID, AllowOpenGOP and MaximizePowerEfficiency are accepted and returned as set; UsingHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder (false) and NumberOfPendingFrames (0) are read-only. Colour names ITU_R_709_2 -> 1, SMPTE_C / ITU_R_601_4 -> 6, anything else -> 2. Wrong CF type -> -12902; unknown keys are kept, stored, answered with success and said on the console (lead c6 change after the phone showed CMCapture sets EncoderUsage/FigThreadPriority/...; this deliberately overrides TASK.md's -12900); unset key -> -12783.
copySupportedPropertyDictionary: 29 entries, each {PropertyType: Number|Boolean|Enumeration, ReadWriteStatus: ReadWrite|ReadOnly}, returned +1.

encodeFrame: mutex-serialised; validates image, pixel format (420v/420f/y420) and session size, emitting exactly one -12902 with a NULL sample on every rejection; locks the pixel buffer read-only on all paths; lazily opens n2avc on the first picture so properties set after startSession count; creates the format description from n2avc's own SPS/PPS with 4-byte NAL length; copies each AVCC packet into an owning CMBlockBuffer; CMSampleBufferCreateReady with duration/pts/dts=pts; NotSync/DependsOnOthers attachments; emits once with status 0; sets *infoFlagsOut = 0. n2avc/open/header failures emit one -12912 with a NULL sample and a single log line.
completeFrames returns 0 (encoding is synchronous); finalize closes n2avc, releases the format description and property values and destroys the mutex.
vt/symbols.txt: every system symbol n2avc_vt.c imports, with the image that exports it (CF, CoreMedia, CoreVideo, VideoToolbox, libSystem pthread/memset).

vt/test_avc_vt/stub_n2avc.c: n2avc.h test double. One 20-byte AVCC sample per picture (4-byte big-endian length 16 + 16-byte NAL carrying picture index 0..N in bytes 4..7); fixed SPS {67 42 C0 1E D9 00} and PPS {68 CE 3C 80}; records config, reconfigure calls, close count, and can inject an open failure or one encode failure.

vt/test_avc_vt/t_avc_vt.c: literal-oracle host suite (see commands). Real-encoder branch converts the concatenated AVCC samples to Annex B (SPS/PPS prepended), runs ffmpeg and requires exactly 10 decoded 176x144 pictures.

vt/test_avc_vt/run_tests.sh: ASan+UBSan stub build/run, TSan stub build/run, then the real avc/ build/run when avc/*.c exists and compiles; last line N2TEST WP05 PASS n/n. The supported-property dictionary is exercised through WP02's n2fake_session_vtable/encoder accessors.

A forced real-encoder run (WP05_REAL=1) proved the integration up to the encoder core: n2avc_open accepted the config built from the defaults (640x480, 30/1, CQP 26, four slices, keyint 60, flags 0), n2avc_headers returned SPS/PPS, and CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromH264ParameterSets succeeded; the first n2avc_encode then aborted inside WP03's n2avc_intra_mb, which is reported as WP03's bug.

The real-encoder acceptance now passes end to end with the lead's avc2 core (avc2/n2avc_core.c + the pinned avc2/n2avc_inter.c/n2avc_me.c/n2avc_rc.c): 10 frames 176x144 through the VideoToolbox object, AVCC converted to Annex B by the test, ffmpeg with empty stderr and exactly 10 decoded 176x144 pictures; the 305 real-branch checks also cover 640x480, timing, attachments, ForceKeyFrame and the format description.
The 640x480 stub check accepts a chain of AVCC 4-byte lengths (not only one NAL per sample), per the lead's edit, so the real multi-slice stream is checked completely; 310 real checks now.

Lead edits integrated in the glue (c6-c8): unknown properties are logged and kept, start/first-picture/session-end lines include per-session encode timing, and N2AVC_F_DEBLOCK is enabled for width*height <= 1280x720 unless /private/var/db/nord2-video-no-deblock exists (/private/var/db/nord2-video-deblock-all forces it above 720p). The host suite asserts the DEBLOCK bit at 640x480 and with 420f and stays 1056/1056.
not_done: WP03's own avc/ core still produces P-slice CAVLC errors (IDR clean, every P slice adds ffmpeg syntax errors). run_tests.sh therefore prefers avc2/n2avc_core.c when it exists, which it does and which passes; with only avc/ present the real run is still gated on avc/STATUS.json or WP05_REAL=1.
The complete iOS dylib link still depends on the chosen core being included by build_ios.sh; vt/n2avc_vt.c itself compiles for arm64-apple-ios16.0 with zero warnings.
Quality changes after the encoder has been opened are stored but do not change the QP of the running n2avc instance; n2avc_reconfigure only carries bitrate and frame rate.
No phone run of any kind (this package is host-tested and iOS-compile-checked only).

commands.last_line: all imports are listed in vt/symbols.txt; n2avc_* and n2vt_say are internal to the dylib

known_risks: Not proven by the fake: who retains the encoder object and the VTVideoEncoderSession. This glue retains neither the object (VideoToolbox owns it) nor the session token, following TASK.md and the VCH263 shape; if real VideoToolbox expects the encoder to keep a +1 on the session, startSession/encodeFrame will use a dangling token.

Not proven by the fake: whether VTEncoderSessionEmitEncodedFrame may synchronously re-enter the encoder (for example from the client's output callback while encodeFrame still holds the per-encoder mutex). TASK.md requires the mutex across encodeFrame; a re-entrant property call from the callback would deadlock.

Not proven by the fake: the exact strings VideoToolbox and its clients expect in copySupportedPropertyDictionary values ('PropertyType' / 'ReadWriteStatus' / 'Number' / 'Boolean' / 'Enumeration' / 'ReadWrite' / 'ReadOnly'). The keys themselves follow TASK.md.
Not proven by the fake: that a sync frame with kCMSampleAttachmentKey_NotSync explicitly set to kCFBooleanFalse is accepted; TASK.md permits absent or false and the test accepts both.
Not proven by the fake: whether VideoToolbox always passes non-NULL pts and duration. The glue substitutes {0,1,valid,0} for a NULL pointer instead of dereferencing it.

Not proven by the fake: whether a client may change pixel format between 420v and 420f mid-session. The first picture fixes n2avc_config.flags (N2AVC_F_FULLRANGE for 420f) and a later change is rejected with one -12912 emit, because the SPS VUI range cannot change inside one stream.

Not proven by the fake: whether VideoToolbox sets AverageBitRate/ExpectedFrameRate after startSession but before the first frame; the lazy n2avc_open makes those values reach the config, which the stub test verifies.

Not proven by the fake: whether n2avc emits a new SPS/PPS mid-stream. The format description is built once from the first successful picture and reused; a changing SPS would make later samples inconsistent.
Policy choice: DataRateLimits with no AverageBitRate uses the first bytes/seconds pair as the target bitrate (a cap with no average would otherwise be unenforceable in constant-QP mode).

Policy choice: MaxKeyFrameInterval 0 is passed to n2avc as 0, which n2avc.h documents as its default 60; MaxKeyFrameIntervalDuration is converted with the frame rate known at open time, and the smaller non-zero interval wins.

The fake's CMSampleBuffer is not a real CoreMedia object; ownership of the CMBlockBuffer/sample buffer after a successful emit is modelled as VideoToolbox retaining the sample and the glue releasing its own references immediately, as TASK.md specifies.
The real encoder path depends on WP03's n2avc_reconfigure accepting the same (bitrate, fps_num, fps_den) contract; the stub only proves the glue calls it once per relevant change.

NumberOfSlices/N2Threads changes after the encoder has been opened are stored but only take effect at the next open: n2avc_reconfigure carries bitrate and frame rate only, and n2avc has no re-slice call.

The real branch currently links the lead's avc2 core with the pinned avc2 copies of WP04's files, not WP03's avc/ core; the glue interface exercised is identical, but a WP03-only build would still fail on WP03's CAVLC bugs.

Our startSession accepts 4096x2304 at any frame rate up to the property limit, as TASK.md requires, but the current avc2 core refuses that size at 30 fps (pick_level MaxMBPS); the first encodeFrame then emits one -12912. This is a core contract issue reported by WP03, not a glue path; at the sizes Camera uses (720p/1080p) the real test passes.

WP03's allocator interposition found per-P-picture calloc in WP04's n2avc_inter.c/n2avc_me.c reached through n2avc_encode. The glue itself allocates only the owning CMBlockBuffer/CMSampleBuffer per emitted frame (required by VideoToolbox), but on the phone the WP04 allocations are in mediaserverd's frame path and may cost time.

External observation (lead's board post, not a WP05 run): stage 1 is reported working on the phone through stock VideoToolbox with this glue -- n2avc at 640x480 5.6 ms/picture, 1280x720 12.7 ms, 1920x1080 23.1 ms, and AVAssetWriter/AVAssetReader H.264+AAC round trip. This package itself never touched the phone and claims no phone result.

The deblocking choice reads /private/var/db switches from inside build_config (lead edit); on the host those paths do not exist, so the host tests always see deblocking on. This does not model a phone where the switch files are present differently; the phone log's 'deblock N' field is the observation to check.

TASK.md says an unknown property must return N2_kVTPropertyNotSupportedErr; the lead's c6 change instead keeps it and returns success because mediaserverd/CMCapture set keys that are not in our table and refusing them can stop a recording. The host test asserts the new behaviour and the log line.
